title: PhotoId-Whale: Blue Whale Dorsal Fin Classification for Mobile Devices
author: Rosa I Ramos-Arredondo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be2rjgd6

steps.title: Obtain Image
steps.instruction: Acquire the image to be classified from the database or from field collection.

steps.title: Perform ROI Selection and Extraction
steps.instruction: Isolate the dorsal fin from the image background using a two-substage process.

substeps.instruction: Indicate the initial point in the dorsal fin area via a graphical interface based on established criteria to select the Region of Interest (ROI).
Extract the dorsal fin from the image background to obtain the segmented ROI contour.

steps.title: Extract Main Characteristics
steps.instruction: Implement Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) on the contour of the dorsal fin obtained from the ROI extraction.

steps.title: Prepare Training Dataset
steps.instruction: Select a representative group of images from the database for system training.

substeps.instruction: Randomly select 20 images from each of the following six classes: right falcate, left falcate, right hook, left hook, right triangular, and left triangular.

steps.title: Calculate Training Weights
steps.instruction: Add weights to the descriptors of each class in the training samples.

substeps.instruction: Calculate weights using the contrast change value of the dorsal fin contour image (z), the number of samples per class (N), and the specific class index (j).

steps.title: Perform Image Matching and Classification
steps.instruction: Determine the number of matching points between the sample image (post-ROI selection) and the training samples for each class.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the number of intersections using the norm of the Euclidean distance between two samples.
Determine the ordinate using the minimum distance between samples.
Utilize the vector position value in the image at different scales L(j, x, y, σ), where x and y are coordinates of the vector at the current training position and ||L2|| is the norm of the vector L2.
